topic: Array.prototype.sort() default order compares numbers as strings: pass a compare function
text:
[1, 30, 4, 21, 100000].sort() returns [1, 100000, 21, 30, 4].

No bug in the engine. Without a compare function, JavaScript converts every element to a string and compares UTF-16 code units. So "100000" lands before "21", and "30" before "4".

The fix is one argument:

arr.sort((a, b) => a - b)

This returns [1, 4, 21, 30, 100000]. Swap a and b for descending order.

Two more things from the MDN docs:
- sort() mutates the array in place, so copy first (or use toSorted()).
- The subtraction trick doesn't work if the array contains NaN.

Takeaway: for anything that isn't a plain string, always pass a compare function.
